chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: In this book I will argue that the trends listed above, and many others, are indeed interrelated.
text_raw:
In this book I will argue that the trends listed above, and many

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Analysis by my colleagues and me of historical states shows that complex, large-scale human societies tend to go through cycles of alternating integrative and disintegrative phases.
text_raw:
Analysis by my colleagues and me of
historical states shows that complex, large-scale human societies
tend to go through cycles of alternating integrative and disintegrative
phases.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Long periods of relative equity, prosperity, and internal peace are succeeded by periods of inequity, immiseration, and political instability, frequently ending in state collapses, revolutions, and civil wars.
text_raw:
Long periods of relative equity, prosperity, and internal
peace are succeeded by periods of inequity, immiseration, and
political instability, frequently ending in state collapses, revolutions,
and civil wars.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Each of the â€œsecularâ€ phases, integrative and disintegrative, unfolds over several human generations.
text_raw:
Each of the â€œsecularâ€ phases, integrative and
disintegrative, unfolds over several human generations.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: The typical period of the overall secular cycle is around two centuries, although there is a lot of variability, depending on the type of society in question, starting conditions, and chance events.
text_raw:
The typical
period of the overall secular cycle is around two centuries, although
there is a lot of variability, depending on the type of society in
question, starting conditions, and chance events.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: What is particularly relevant to the questions with which I started this Preface, is that while post-crisis dynamics can take many routes, the pre-crisis periods tend to have the same characteristic features, shared across many societies and even different historical eras.
text_raw:
What is particularly relevant to the questions with which I
started this Preface, is that while post-crisis dynamics can take many
routes, the pre-crisis periods tend to have the same characteristic
features, shared across many societies and even different historical
eras.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: The American polity today has a lot in common with the Antebellum America of the 1850s; with Ancien Regime France on the eve of the French Revolution; with Stuart England during the 1630s; and innumerable other historical societies that went through integrative/disintegrative cycles.
text_raw:
The American polity today has a lot in common with the
Antebellum America of the 1850s; with Ancien Regime France on
the eve of the French Revolution; with Stuart England during the
1630s; and innumerable other historical societies that went through
integrative/disintegrative cycles.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Can it really be true that the troubles of our days are not so new, and many historical societies
text_raw:
Can it really be true that the troubles
of our days are not so new, and many historical societies

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: experienced them previously?
text_raw: experienced them previously?

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: I will marshal empirically supported theory and a lot of data to show that this is, indeed, the case.
text_raw:
I will marshal empirically supported
theory and a lot of data to show that this is, indeed, the case.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: However, unlike historical societies, we are in a unique position to take steps that could allow us to escape the worst.
text_raw:
However, unlike historical societies, we are in a unique position
to take steps that could allow us to escape the worst.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Societal breakdown and ensuing waves of violence can be avoided by collective, cooperative action.
text_raw:
Societal
breakdown and ensuing waves of violence can be avoided by
collective, cooperative action.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: My goal is to present in this book the best current understanding of why political violence in states waxes and wanes in long cycles.
text_raw:
My goal is to present in this book the
best current understanding of why political violence in states waxes
and wanes in long cycles.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: This understanding is encapsulated in what has become known as Structural-Demographic Theory (SDT), whose empirical adequacy has been tested on a number of historical societies.
text_raw:
This understanding is encapsulated in
what has become known as Structural-Demographic Theory (SDT),
whose empirical adequacy has been tested on a number of historical
societies.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: As we shall see in this book, the SDT helps us answer why the various trends mentioned earlier changed direction from favorable to unfavorable in America around the 1970s.
text_raw:
As we shall see in this book, the SDT helps us answer why
the various trends mentioned earlier changed direction from
favorable to unfavorable in America around the 1970s.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Such understanding is the key to developing reforms that would reverse these negative trends, and move us to a more equitable, prosperous, and peaceful society.
text_raw:
Such
understanding is the key to developing reforms that would reverse
these negative trends, and move us to a more equitable, prosperous,

text: Second, rapid expansion of population results in elite overproduction â€”an increased number of aspirants for the limited supply of elite positions.

text: Large complex models not only require many arbitrary decisions and the estimation of a multitude of difficult-to-measure parameters, they also tend to be structurally unstable, so that a small change in one parameter value results in a large change in the dynamics of the model.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: For this reason, the only feasible way to deal with such complex systems is to build a spectrum of models, each addressing a somewhat different aspect of the problem, and each simple enough to avoid the pitfalls of large, unwieldy models (large parameter numbers and structural instability).
